data.name: AttackerKey

data.name: AttackerPad
data.value: The generator and the attacker share a secret pad (128 bits). Whoever learns the pad (by taking the device apart) can read all keys: this is the weakness against the SETUP attack, where the generator knows only the public key.

data.name: Conclusion
data.value: Without the secret exponent d, n looks random and is as hard to factor as any other modulus. So the backdoor cannot be found by looking at the keys, only by examining the generator itself. The four methods of the settings show the honest generation, two places for the hidden value and the difference between a public-key and a shared-secret backdoor. Real SETUP attacks use elliptic curves to hide more bits.

data.name: Intro
data.value: A changed key generator (a smart card, a library) makes RSA keys that look normal. Without it nobody sees the difference, but the attacker, who knows a secret key, can factor every public key it makes. Small numbers are used here.
